The patient's payer applies its two-midnight inpatient rule when the treating physician expects hospital-level treatment to span at least two midnights. Our utilization review portal confirms that this case qualifies for inpatient status if that expected stay is documented.

transcript.text:
Thank you all for that critical information. Let me summarize what I've heard and how it factors into my decision:

Dr. Alvarez, your clinical finding of intermittent pauses on the rhythm strip that are unsafe without continuous telemetry for 24 hours is a key medical factor. This supports the need for continued cardiac monitoring.

Maya, your utilization review information is very helpful — the payer's two-midnight rule means inpatient status requires documented expectation of a stay spanning at least two midnights.

Jon, the patient education scheduling constraint — the daughter can only attend discharge teaching on Friday from 16:30 to 17:00 — is an important logistical consideration for planning the discharge timeline.

Putting this together: Dr. Alvarez's finding of unsafe pauses requiring 24 hours of continuous telemetry, combined with the need to coordinate discharge teaching with the daughter on Friday, suggests a stay that would span at least two midnights. This would support inpatient admission to a telemetry bed under the payer's two-midnight rule.

Unless anyone has additional information or concerns, I'm prepared to finalize the decision as inpatient admission to telemetry with an expected length of stay of two nights, which would allow us to complete the 24-hour monitoring and schedule the discharge teaching on Friday afternoon.
